ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, shareholders and signatories against the UN Consolidated List, UK OFSI consolidated sanctions list, US OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, BVI FSC warning and disciplinary lists, and ICM registry enforcement databases. PEP status is determined under FATF Recommendations 12 and 22; full source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification is required for all PEPs, family members and close associates. Simplified due diligence is not available for corporate formations despite the low-risk commercial tier; all records must be retained for at least 5 years after business relationship termination.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BVI Registry of Corporate Affairs (RoCA) — search and name reservation portal operated via a licensed BVI registered agent
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official registry language is English. The statutory company name must be in Latin script; non-Latin scripts such as Chinese, Cyrillic or Arabic may be used only as a romanized transliteration or secondary trading name. The registered legal name is restricted to Latin letters, Arabic numerals and limited punctuation, must be distinguishable from existing registered names, and must end with an approved type indicator including 'Limited', 'Ltd', 'Corporation', 'Inc.', or an approved BVI abbreviation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a proposed name is rejected, the registered agent must immediately file a new name reservation. A formal administrative appeal may be submitted in writing through the registered agent to the Registrar of Corporate Affairs within 14 days of refusal, asserting that the name is not prohibited, misleading or confusingly similar to an existing name. If the Registrar maintains the rejection, the applicant may apply for judicial review in the BVI High Court, and may in parallel reserve an alternative name to avoid transactional delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not sufficient to satisfy the statutory registered office requirement. Every BVI Business Company must maintain a physical registered office in the BVI at the office of its licensed registered agent. A virtual office may be used solely as an administrative or business service address for e-commerce records and customer correspondence, provided it is distinct from the mandatory BVI registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: estimated 2% to 5% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months for a non-licensed novelty merchandise merchant. The likelihood increases to 10% to 15% if sanctions screening triggers, PEP status, adverse media, FATF jurisdictional concerns, or economic substance filings indicate possible AML abuse or lack of genuine BVI commercial activity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: BVI Business Companies Act, 2004 (as amended), ss. 3, 5, 6, 16 and 60 (incorporation, registered agent/office, memorandum & articles, and commencement); UK Companies Act 2006, Part 34 (ss. 1043-1055) and the Overseas Companies Regulations 2009 (SI 2009/1801), regs. 5-8 (registration of a UK establishment of an overseas company)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registry of Corporate Affairs, BVI Financial Services Commission (formation); Companies House, UK Registrar of Companies (registration of the BVI company's UK establishment)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: BVI: Form BC/1 electronic incorporation application with Memorandum and Articles of Association filed through a licensed registered agent on the VIRRGIN portal; UK: Form OSIN01 (Overseas Company: Particulars of Establishment) together with certified constitutional documents
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow, capital duty or deposit requirement for a BVI Business Company (s. 42); the initial subscriber typically subscribes for one US$1.00 par ordinary share, fully paid in cash; UK Companies House imposes no minimum capital on overseas companies
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by unanimous written consent of the sole incorporator of [BVI Company Name] Limited in lieu of a meeting: (1) the company's incorporation under the BVI Business Companies Act, 2004 is ratified and the filed Memorandum and Articles are adopted; (2) the subscriber's taking of one ordinary share of US$1.00 is approved and recorded in the register of members; (3) [Registered Agent Name] is confirmed as licensed registered agent and its office at [Address, Road Town, Tortola] is adopted as the registered office; (4) [Director Name] is appointed first director and [Officer Name] is appointed secretary, each authorised to open bank accounts and instruct professional advisers; and (5) the director is authorised to execute all UK Companies House registrations and licensing filings.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), an executive department of HM Treasury; principal online portal is GOV.UK (www.gov.uk) with HMRC Online Services for corporate tax and VAT registration, return filing, and Making Tax Digital (MTD) API integration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a BVI Business Company (raw v.s. non-UK resident) selling hard enamel lapel pins: Step 1 — Determine UK nexus: UK Corporation Tax (CT) applies to a non-UK resident company only if it carries on a trade in the UK through a permanent establishment (CTA 2010 ss.5, 15–19); otherwise no UK CT registration or return obligation exists. Step 2 — If a taxable UK permanent establishment is created, the BC must register for CT within 3 months of commencing UK trade by submitting Form CT41G or the online 'register a non-resident company for Corporation Tax' application via HMRC; HMRC issues a 10-digit Unique Taxpayer Reference (UTR). Step 3 — For VAT: if the BC supplies goods from a UK stock to UK consumers via Etsy or Stripe and the consignment value at the point of sale does not exceed £135, the online marketplace is the deemed supplier for VAT and the BC is not separately required to register; if goods are in the UK at the point of sale regardless of marketplace, or UK taxable turnover exceeds £90,000 in a rolling 12-month period, the BC must apply for UK VAT registration electronically (Form VAT1, or VAT2 for non-established businesses), submitting certified incorporation certificate, director identity documents, business plan, bank reference, and overseas tax status evidence; HMRC ordinarily issues the VAT registration number within 15 working days. Step 4 — If no compulsory registration arises, the BC may apply for voluntary VAT registration to recover input VAT on UK inbound costs, subject to HMRC approval and security conditions for non-established businesses.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: UK law does not operate a US-style check-the-box election; entity classification follows domestic jurisprudence and the independent entity status of a BVI BC is respected unless a hybrid mismatch arises under Part 6A TIOPA 2010. Where an entity is hybrid (e.g., one jurisdiction treats it as transparent, the UK treats it as opaque), taxpayers may make a collective election or alignment election with HMRC to eliminate the mismatch, thereby preventing deduction/non-inclusion double-counting; the election is made in the CT return and requires notice to HMRC under TIOPA 2010 s.259RB. VAT-specific elections include: voluntary value-based registration below the £90,000 threshold (VATA 1994 Sch. 1), option to tax land (VATA 1994 Sch. 10) — not applicable to pin sales, VAT grouping for UK group companies (VATA 1994 s.43), and the special 'Overseas Persons' registration under Form VAT2. There is no election for territorial taxation: a BVI BC without a UK permanent establishment is simply outside the UK CT charge.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) — United Kingdom VAT Act 1994 (VATA) and HMRC VAT Notices; customs duties and import VAT apply upon entry into Great Britain under the UK Global Tariff.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: £90,000 (GBP) taxable turnover in any rolling 12-month period; for suppliers established in Northern Ireland making distance sales of goods to EU consumers, a lower £9,000 (GBP) / €10,000 distance-selling threshold applies. A non-established BVI BC is subject to mandatory registration when its UK-taxable turnover exceeds £90,000, when goods are held in a UK fulfilment centre at the point of sale, or when the online marketplace (Etsy) is not the deemed supplier. Voluntary registration is available below the threshold and is commonly used to recover UK input VAT. For consignments sold by an overseas seller to a UK consumer via Etsy with an intrinsic value not exceeding £135, the seller is disregarded for VAT on that supply and the marketplace is the deemed seller under VATA 1994 s.5B.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The UK does not impose a real-time e-invoicing clearance or digital stamping regime comparable to Italy or Spain. Mandatory compliance is instead driven by Making Tax Digital for VAT (MTD): every VAT-registered business must keep digital records and file VAT returns exclusively through HMRC-recognised software or bridging software using HMRC's real-time JSON/REST API endpoints; paper returns or manual portal data entry are prohibited for MTD filings. E-invoices in PEPPOL/UBL or XML formats are legally acceptable, but there is no government fiscal stamp, clearance, or validation service before issuance. For export transactions, the Customs Declaration Service (CDS) is the mandatory digital platform for submitting export declarations to HMRC; CDS messages and Goods Movement Reference (GMR) data are exchanged via API/EDIFACT, and the exporter must retain MRN (Movement Reference Number) evidence.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The supply of hard enamel lapel pins (ISIC 3240) qualifies for the 0% rate as a supply of goods exported to a destination outside the United Kingdom (VATA 1994 s.30 and Sch. 8, Group 8) provided three cumulative conditions are met: (1) the goods are exported by the supplier (or on its behalf) to a non-UK destination, including the USA and third-country markets, at or before the end of the supply; (2) within the required statutory time limit (generally 3 months from the time of supply, or a longer period under HMRC Notice 703 for certain consignment/removal arrangements) the exporter obtains and retains valid commercial, transport, and customs evidence of export; and (3) the goods are not subjected to a subsequent onward supply or use within the UK. Exports via Etsy/Stripe sales and international courier are zero-rated only where the seller, acting as principal, causes the goods to leave the UK and holds the relevant CDS export declaration (MRN), courier airway bill or Bill of Lading, and commercial invoice demonstrating delivery to the overseas buyer. Supplies to Northern Ireland from Great Britain are removals, not exports, and remain within UK VAT rules unless re-sold to EU consumers under the NI distance-selling regime. Services ancillary to the pin export (e.g., ocean/air freight) are zero-rated under Schedule 8, Group 8 items 4–6 if directly linked to export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration filed via the Customs Declaration Service (CDS) — MRN (Movement Reference Number) output, or a full SAD/Form C88 if an oral/express declaration is not used
Bill of Lading (sea freight) or Air Waybill / courier consignment note with tracked delivery proof for exports via Etsy/Stripe postal or parcel routes
Commercial invoice in the exporter's name showing the buyer, Incoterms (recommended FCA or EXW), pin description, quantity, unit price, and 0% VAT entry
Packing list detailing carton weights, pin counts, and destination customs code (HS 7117.90 or 7326.90 jewellery/pins classification)

Evidence of cross-border payment receipt — bank statement, Stripe/Etsy settlement record, or FX inward remittance confirmation from an EMI/neo-bank evidencing proceeds in foreign currency (the UK does not issue a statutory Inward Remittance Certificate; the payment receipt replaces that instrument)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: HMRC may disallow zero-rating and claw back 20% VAT on the full sales value where the prescribed export evidence is not obtained, retained for six years, and produced on demand (VAT Notice 703 and Regulations 34–38 of the VAT Regulations 1995); the assessment window is generally 4 years, extended to 20 years for dishonesty or deliberate concealment (VATA 1994 s.77). Penalties for inaccurate tax documents are charged under Schedule 24 Finance Act 2007: up to 30% of the presumed VAT loss for careless errors and 100% for deliberate and concealed errors; failure-to-keep-records penalties under Schedule 26 Finance Act 2007 carry daily fines up to £500/day; unpaid VAT attracts interest under the Finance Act 1995 plus late-payment penalties of 0–15% under Schedule 24 equivalent rules. Where a purported export is diverted back into the UK or used to create an MTIC/carousel chain, criminal liability arises under VATA 1994 s.72 with up to 7 years' imprisonment, unlimited fines, and a mandatory surcharge; HMRC can withdraw the 0% rating, issue jeopardy assessments, and hold directors personally liable under a deemed-controller or facilitation test. Although the UK imposes no statutory FX-repatriation deadline, the 180-day benchmark adopted for this pipeline follows the standard cross-border settlement cycle of Etsy Direct Pay and Stripe; any payment remaining abroad beyond that window without satisfactory evidence is treated by HMRC as a diversion risk in an export zero-rating audit.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England (BoE) acts as the monetary authority and lender of last resort; HM Treasury, the Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation (OFSI) and HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC) jointly administer financial sanctions, AML/CFT and tax reporting. There is no dedicated UK foreign-exchange-control authority since the repeal of the Exchange Control Act 1979; the UK operates a fully liberalised capital account without a requirement for FX approvals.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The UK offers unrestricted current-account and capital-account convertibility for GBP, USD, EUR and CNY transactions. A BVI Business Company may freely remit dividend, interest, royalty, loan repayment and liquidation proceeds to or from the United Kingdom, subject only to OFSI sanctions screening, HMRC corporate tax filing (if the BVI BC creates a UK permanent establishment) and the requirements of the Economic Crime (Transparency and Enforcement) Act 2022. No central bank approval is required for profit repatriation, and there are no surrender or mandatory conversion obligations for a BVI BC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. UK law and BoE policy impose no statutory surrender timelines, no minimum conversion ratios and no obligation to surrender export proceeds. A BVI BC may invoice in any freely usable currency (GBP, USD, EUR or CNY), retain export receipts in any bank account, and utilise those funds directly for disbursement to suppliers or reinvestment. The only ancillary obligations are HMRC customs entry declarations, Intrastat reporting thresholds, and Common Reporting Standard disclosures if the BVI BC is considered a UK-managed entity.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium. UK-authorised Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) such as Airwallex, Currencycloud and Wise Business will accept a BVI Business Company only when the BVI entity provides a valid BVI registration number, audited financial statements (if trading), a real-office substance declaration, and clear source of wealth for the shareholder. Legal constraints under the UK Electronic Money Regulations 2011 and JMLSG require EMIs to conduct enhanced due diligence (EDD) on all non-UK tax-resident corporate clients. Low acceptance for Stripe Treasury and Revolut Business because they mandate a UK-incorporated entity or a UK resident director; however, payments via Stripe (card acquirer) are permissible as a payment channel without opening a UK bank account, as long as the BVI BC is linked to a USD bank account in an OECD white-list jurisdiction.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is expressly permitted by the UK Financial Conduct Authority under the FCA CASS and Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing and Transfer of Funds (Information on the Payer) Regulations 2019. A physical appearance is not a statutory mandate. Nevertheless, Tier-1 UK banks routinely require a live video KYC interview with all directors and shareholders, passport and driver's-licence certification by an overseas notary, a banker's reference from the BVI introducing institution, and a certified copy of the BVI Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing. If the BVI BC shows adverse risk indicators (e.g., nominee directors or trust ownership), the bank may require a physical interview at a UK branch or at a UK consulate in the director's jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: BVI offshore jurisdiction flag: the UK bank's automated system treats a BVI Company as a non-EEA offshore vehicle with higher money-laundering risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) BVI Certificate of Incorporation; (2) BVI Certificate of Good Standing dated within 3 months; (3) BVI Register of Directors and Register of Members; (4) UBO Declaration signed by each beneficial owner; (5) No-liability Certificate from BVI Registry; (6) A formal letter of introduction from a licensed BVI registered agent (e.g., Trident Trust, Maples).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex group ownership: the BVI BC is 100% owned by another BVI BC or trust with no natural-person disclosure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) complete chain-of-title chart from the ultimate natural person to the BVI BC; (2) certified passports and proof of residential address for all UBOs; (3) trust deed or foundation charter, if any; (4) high-street certified translation of all non-English documents; (5) an external legal opinion from a UK-qualified lawyer confirming that the ownership structure is not intended to conceal money laundering or tax evasion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-ticket B2C payments from Etsy and Stripe: UK AML teams may view recurring micro-payments from card networks as indicators of front-running or unlicensed money-service business activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) signed commercial supply agreements with Etsy Marketplace and Stripe; (2) a realistic business plan forecasting projected monthly transaction volume, average ticket size and refund rate; (3) product-sourcing invoices and customs declarations for brass and enamel raw materials; (4) proof of marketplace registration (shop URL) and full traceability of order IDs; (5) annual audited accounts or a certified management accountant statement proving the transaction cycle is a genuine sale of goods.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/counterparty risk: suppliers or customers located in China (PRC) or Hong Kong with payments routed through USD or CNY clearing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) OFSI sanctions screening of all counterparties via a recognised vendor (Dow Jones, LexisNexis, World-Check); (2) commercial invoices from PRC suppliers with the exact goods description (ISIC 3240 – die-struck enamel pins); (3) bill of lading / air waybill; (4) a certificate of origin from the supplier's customs authority; (5) a statement from the BVI BC director confirming no dealings with listed terrorist entities, military end-users or nuclear/proliferation programs.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The BVI BC's shareholder (e.g., a Hong Kong or UK holding entity) injects equity or sends a subordinated loan to the UK bank account via SWIFT MT103. Use purpose code 'DCB' (Direct Investment Equity) for equity injections or 'CLA' (Intercompany Loan) for loan advances. The SWIFT field 70 should mention 'Equity Injection into BVI BC for Working Capital – ISIC 3240' or 'Loan per Intercompany Agreement dated [YYYY-MM-DD]'. The UK bank will screen the payment against OFSI/OFAC lists; because the BVI BC is not UK tax resident, no UK withholding tax is deducted on the inbound wire. If the inbound amount exceeds GBP 100,000, the UK receiving bank will automatically file a BOP return to the Bank of England within 2 business days. No clearance or prior approval is needed from the BoE or HM Treasury.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For payment to enamel-pin manufacturers (typically PRC/HK suppliers) and freight forwarders, the BVI BC will issue SWIFT MT103 instructions from its UK bank account with UETR (Unique End-to-End Transaction Reference). For letters of credit, an MT700 documentary LC may be established with the BVI BC as applicant and the PRC supplier as beneficiary. Payments should be routed in USD, CNY or GBP via the UK's Faster Payments / CHAPS (GBP), or via CNAPS (CNY) using a PBOC-cleared correspondent bank in London (e.g., Standard Chartered, HSBC). The UK bank will require underlying commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading and a copy of the ISIC 3240 manufacturing contract to satisfy the 'Trade Services - Export/Import' classification. There is no FX surrender restriction, but use of a documented forward contract is recommended to hedge CNY/USD volatility.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (GBP/USD, USD/CNY and GBP/CNY) up to 12 months tenor, available from Tier-1 UK banks on a covered OTC basis.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on offshore CNY (USD/CNH) executed in London market referencing the CNH spot rate, given the non-convertibility of CNY in mainland China.
Cross-currency swaps (fixed-floating GBP/USD, USD/CNY, EUR/USD) used to hedge multi-currency loan or supply-chain exposures over a 2-5 year horizon.
European-style FX options (GBP/USD, EUR/USD, USD/CNH) purchased for downside protection on trade receivables denominated in USD or EUR.
Rolling spot FX forwards (4-day forward) available through UK EMIs (Airwallex, Currencycloud) for smaller-value high-frequency disbursements to Etsy settlement accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BVI Annual Government License Fee / Registered Agent Renewal Remittance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BVI Registry of Corporate Affairs / Financial Services Commission, via the BVI Registered Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Invoiced on 1 January; due no later than 31 May of the calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late fee per month or part of a month after 31 May; continued arrearage after 12 months exposes the company to administrative strike-off and dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BVI Annual Return (post-2022 amendment) with prescribed particulars of shareholders, directors, shares, and financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BVI Registry of Corporate Affairs (Financial Services Commission) through the BOSS online portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 9 months after each financial year-end (e.g., 30 September for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: US$300 late filing penalty after the initial grace period, with escalating monthly default penalties of US$100; repeated non-compliance may lead to regulatory warning and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BVI Economic Substance Notification (ESN) or Annual Economic Substance Return when applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BVI International Tax Authority (ITA) within the Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after financial year-end for notification (e.g., 30 June for a 31 December year-end); 12 months for a full economic substance return if the company is tax resident in the BVI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fixed penalties up to US$500, daily default penalties up to US$250, and potential strike-off for material non-compliance; directors and officers may also face personal fines.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is required for this standard, unregulated Tax-Exempt BVI Business Company. A compulsory independent audit applies only if the BVI company is (1) licensed and regulated by the BVI Financial Services Commission; (2) tax-resident in the BVI for Economic Substance purposes and carrying on a relevant activity; or (3) listed on a recognised stock exchange. Under the stated ISIC 3240 enamel-pins sales activity, no BVI audit threshold is crossed.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: The BVI Business Companies Act prescribes no formal reporting framework for an unregulated, non-audited company; IFRS is the market standard for any voluntarily prepared financial statements. If the entity were to establish a UK taxable presence, Companies Act 2006 / FRS 102 would become the applicable framework for UK filing.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The BVI registered agent must complete and submit the annual confirmation through the BVI Beneficial Ownership Secure Search (BOSS) system at the time the Annual Return is filed; the confirmation attests that beneficial ownership information remains accurate. Any share-transfer or UBO change occurring during the year must be uploaded immediately and is then reconciled with the subsequent annual confirmation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Members' and Directors' Meetings
Beneficial Ownership Regime (BOSS) statement held by the Registered Agent

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$600 - US$1,500 per annum for a standard BVI full-service registered agent and office package
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable - no statutory audit; voluntary prepared-audit market range US$3,000 - US$8,000 if a formal opinion is later required

stage_6.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (main rate FY2024, profits > £250,000); 19% small profits rate (profits ≤ £50,000); marginal relief between £50,000 and £250,000
stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Patent Box 10%; R&D tax relief enhanced deductions (up to 27%); 100% full expensing on qualifying plant & machinery; Annual Investment Allowance £1,000,000; 19% Small Profits Rate; marginal relief for mid-sized profits
stage_6.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (indefinite carryforward of trading losses, subject to the £5,000,000 deductions allowance and 50% restriction on excess profits)
